observation.visible_scene: A low-angle view across a calm, glassy body of water on a clear day. The bright sun sits in the upper-left corner, producing strong glare and a small green lens-flare dot in the lower-right. A clump of tall reeds/grasses occupies the left foreground, backlit and partly silhouetted, with one long bent stalk arching out over the water near the bottom edge. A thin distant shoreline with low hills runs across the middle-right under a blue sky containing a small cluster of white clouds near the center. Cloud and sky reflections are visible on the water surface in the lower portion of the frame.
visible_changes: The image is in sharp focus at the start (frames 1-4), then goes noticeably out of focus / soft-blurred through the middle (frames 5-8), and returns to sharp focus from frame 9 onward; this is a focus change rather than object or camera motion.

The overall framing stays essentially fixed: the sun, horizon line, foreground reeds and the arched stalk keep the same positions relative to the frame edges throughout, indicating no significant camera pan or zoom.
Subtle, continuous shimmering of the water surface and its cloud reflections is visible across the clip.
Minor apparent movement of the thin reed tips and the small cloud cluster may be present but is hard to confirm against the focus changes and compression.
outside_clip_unknowns: The cause of the temporary defocus (manual focus pull, autofocus hunt, or a cut) is not shown.
Whether the reeds are swaying from wind, and the broader context before and after this excerpt, are not visible.
uncertain_details: Slow drift of the clouds and any gentle sway of the reeds are not reliably distinguishable from the blur transition and frame-to-frame noise.
The exact moment of the focus transition is approximate (between frame 4 and 5, and between frame 8 and 9).
